subproblem.title: Transfer of parameter-a.e. properties to H^n-a.e. points of a set covered by Lipschitz pieces
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel, F_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^P (i ∈ ℕ) Lipschitz maps, and B_i ⊆ ℝ^n arbitrary sets with H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n]. Let p be any property of points of ℝ^P such that, for every i, p(F_i(b)) holds for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B_i (∀ᵐ b ∂(volume⌞B_i)). Then p(x) holds for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n]⌞M)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (F : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (p : Euclid P → Prop), MeasurableSet M → (∀ i, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (F i)) → μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, F i '' B i) = 0 → (∀ i, ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict (B i)), p (F i b)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), p x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (H^n(F_i(N_i)) ≤ L_i^n λ(N_i) = 0 and the inclusion of the exceptional set in Z ∪ ⋃_i F_i(N_i)), stated for an arbitrary property p; details filled in. λ := volume (Lebesgue measure) on ℝ^n.
1. Exceptional parameters. Fix i and put N_i := {b ∈ B_i : p(F_i b) fails}. From ∀ᵐ b ∂(λ⌞B_i), p(F_i b) we get ∀ᵐ b ∂λ, (b ∈ B_i → p(F_i b)) (ae_imp_of_ae_restrict; no measurability of B_i or of p is needed: take a measurable λ⌞B_i-null set T ⊇ {b : ¬p(F_i b)}; then λ(T ∩ B_i) = (λ⌞B_i)(T) = 0 and the exceptional set is contained in T ∩ B_i). By ae_iff this says λ({b : ¬(b ∈ B_i → p(F_i b))}) = 0. Every b ∈ N_i lies in that set, so λ(N_i) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
2. Null images. Let L_i be a Lipschitz constant of F_i. On ℝ^n, μHE[n] = λ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so μHE[n](N_i) = 0. By definition μHE[n] = c·μH[n] with c := addHaarScalarFactor(λ, μH[n]) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def; the same constant c is used on ℝ^n and on ℝ^P), and c ≠ 0 (Measure.addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero). Hence μH[n](N_i) = 0. By LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (exponent n ≥ 0), μH[n](F_i(N_i)) ≤ L_i^n μH[n](N_i) = 0, so μHE[n](F_i(N_i)) = c·0 = 0.
3. Covering the exceptional set. Let x ∈ M with p(x) false. If x ∉ ⋃_i F_i(B_i), then x ∈ M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i). Otherwise x = F_i(b) for some i and some b ∈ B_i; then p(F_i b) fails, so b ∈ N_i and x ∈ F_i(N_i). Hence {x : ¬(x ∈ M → p(x))} = {x ∈ M : ¬p(x)} ⊆ (M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) ∪ ⋃_i F_i(N_i).
4. The right-hand side of step 3 is μHE[n]-null: the first set by hypothesis, each F_i(N_i) by step 2, and a countable union and a finite union of null sets are null (measure_iUnion_null, measure_union_null). By monotonicity μHE[n]({x : ¬(x ∈ M → p(x))}) = 0, i.e. ∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], x ∈ M → p(x).
5. Since M is Borel, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n]⌞M), p(x) is equivalent to ∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], x ∈ M → p(x) (ae_restrict_iff'), which is step 4. The argument is uniform in n ≥ 0 and P ≥ 0 (for n = 0, λ on ℝ^0 is the unit point mass, so λ-null sets are empty, and μHE[0] = μH[0]).
proof_key_steps: From the restricted a.e. hypothesis, N_i = {b ∈ B_i : ¬p(F_i b)} is Lebesgue-null (ae_imp_of_ae_restrict, ae_iff).
μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n and μHE[n] = c·μH[n] with c ≠ 0, so the Lipschitz Hausdorff bound gives μHE[n](F_i(N_i)) = 0.
Every x ∈ M where p fails lies in (M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) ∪ ⋃_i F_i(N_i), a countable union of μHE[n]-null sets.
M is Borel, so ae_restrict_iff' converts this into ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n]⌞M), p x.

audit.reason: The arbitrary sets B_i and property p require no unstated measurability: ae_imp_of_ae_restrict gives null exceptional parameter sets. The nonzero Hausdorff normalization and Lipschitz bound give null images. The explicit exceptional-set inclusion and countable union argument prove the result, with Borel measurability of M correctly used for ae_restrict_iff'.

subproblem.title: The chosen approximate tangent plane equals any approximate tangent plane
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, x ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P. If Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), with η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^n = μHE[n]), then approxTangentPlane n M x = Q, where approxTangentPlane n M x is the contract's choice: a chosen plane Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' if such a plane exists, and ⊥ otherwise.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → approxTangentPlane n M x = Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the identification Q(F_i b) = range DF_i(b) by Exists.choose_spec and uniqueness), i.e. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1) (uniqueness of the approximate tangent space), applied to the contract's choice function. No hypothesis on M, x, n or P is used.
1. Definition. In GMT/Ch07/Contract.lean, approxTangentPlane n M x is defined (classically) as h.choose if h : ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' holds, and as ⊥ otherwise.
2. The condition holds. From hQ : HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q we get h := ⟨Q, hQ⟩ : ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q'. Unfolding approxTangentPlane and taking the positive branch of the dependent if-then-else (rw [dite_eq_left h]; dite_eq_left is the current name of the deprecated dif_pos) gives approxTangentPlane n M x = h.choose.
3. The chosen plane is an approximate tangent plane. By Exists.choose_spec, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x h.choose.
4. Uniqueness. SimonGMT's Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1)) states: if HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₁ and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₂, then Q₁ = Q₂. (Its proof: the limits ∫_{Q₁} f dH^n and ∫_{Q₂} f dH^n of the same net coincide for every f ∈ C_c, so H^n⌞Q₁ = H^n⌞Q₂ as regular measures, and the support of H^n⌞Q_k is Q_k because finrank Q_k = n.) It needs no further hypotheses on Euclid P. Applied to step 3 and hQ it gives h.choose = Q.
5. By steps 2 and 4, approxTangentPlane n M x = Q.
proof_key_steps: The hypothesis provides the witness ⟨Q, hQ⟩ of the existential in approxTangentPlane, so the definition returns the chosen plane h.choose.
Exists.choose_spec: h.choose is an approximate tangent plane of M at x.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type match. The tangent hypothesis supplies the existential witness, choose_spec supplies the chosen plane's tangent property, and the pinned uniqueness theorem identifies it with Q without additional hypotheses. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Composing a bi-Lipschitz immersed piece with a bi-Lipschitz immersion of ℝ^P
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n, m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for all a, a' ∈ B, and F differentiable with injective derivative DF(a) at every a ∈ B. Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be differentiable everywhere with Dφ(x) injective for every x, Λ-Lipschitz and Λ'-antilipschitz (|x − y| ≤ Λ'|φ(x) − φ(y)|). Then (i) φ∘F is (ΛL)-Lipschitz; (ii) there is m' > 0 with m'|a − a'| ≤ |φ(F(a)) − φ(F(a'))| for all a, a' ∈ B; (iii) for every a ∈ B, φ∘F is differentiable at a and D(φ∘F)(a) is injective; (iv) for every a ∈ B, range D(φ∘F)(a) = Dφ(F(a))(range DF(a)) (as linear subspaces of ℝ^P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L Λ Λ' : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ F a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ F a)) → Differentiable ℝ φ → (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ φ x)) → LipschitzWith Λ φ → AntilipschitzWith Λ' φ → LipschitzWith (Λ * L) (φ ∘ F) ∧ (∃ m' : ℝ, 0 < m' ∧ ∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m' * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖(φ ∘ F) a - (φ ∘ F) a'‖) ∧ (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ (φ ∘ F) a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (φ ∘ F) a)) ∧ ∀ a ∈ B, LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (φ ∘ F) a : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) = Submodule.map (fderiv ℝ φ (F a) : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F a : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: first half of step 4 of the parent proof (Φ_i := φ∘F_i satisfies the hypotheses of the density lemma, and range DΦ_i(b) = Dφ(F_i b)(range DF_i(b))), with the details filled in. The parent normalises Λ ≥ 1 and uses the constant m/Λ; here m' := m/(Λ' + 1) avoids the normalisation and also covers Λ' = 0.
1. (i) For all a, a' ∈ ℝ^n, |φ(F a) − φ(F a')| ≤ Λ|F a − F a'| ≤ ΛL|a − a'|, so φ∘F is ΛL-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp, which yields exactly the constant Λ * L).
2. (ii) Put m' := m/(Λ' + 1); m' > 0 because m > 0 and Λ' ≥ 0. Let a, a' ∈ B. The antilipschitz bound (AntilipschitzWith.le_mul_dist, with dist = norm of the difference) gives |F a − F a'| ≤ Λ'|φ(F a) − φ(F a')| ≤ (Λ' + 1)|φ(F a) − φ(F a')|. Hence m|a − a'| ≤ |F a − F a'| ≤ (Λ' + 1)|φ(F a) − φ(F a')|, and dividing by Λ' + 1 > 0 gives m'|a − a'| ≤ |φ(F a) − φ(F a')| = |(φ∘F)(a) − (φ∘F)(a')|.
3. (iii) Let a ∈ B. F is differentiable at a and φ is differentiable at F(a), so by the chain rule φ∘F is differentiable at a (DifferentiableAt.comp) with D(φ∘F)(a) = Dφ(F a) ∘L DF(a) (fderiv_comp). As a function this composite is Dφ(F a) ∘ DF(a) (ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp), a composition of the injective maps DF(a) (hypothesis on B) and Dφ(F a) (hypothesis for every x), hence injective (Function.Injective.comp).
4. (iv) Let a ∈ B. By step 3 and ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_comp, the linear map underlying D(φ∘F)(a) is (Dφ(F a) as a linear map) ∘ₗ (DF(a) as a linear map), and for linear maps range(g ∘ₗ f) = map g (range f) (LinearMap.range_comp). Hence range D(φ∘F)(a) = Submodule.map Dφ(F a) (range DF(a)).
proof_key_steps: Lipschitz constants multiply under composition: φ∘F is ΛL-Lipschitz.
The antilipschitz bound |F a − F a'| ≤ Λ'|φF a − φF a'| yields the lower constant m' = m/(Λ' + 1) > 0 on B.
Chain rule at a ∈ B: D(φ∘F)(a) = Dφ(F a)∘DF(a), injective as a composite of injective maps.
range(Dφ(F a)∘DF(a)) = Dφ(F a)(range DF(a)) by toLinearMap_comp and LinearMap.range_comp.

audit.reason: The four conclusions exactly match the prose. The explicit positive constant m/(Λ'+1) handles zero antilipschitz constants. Differentiability hypotheses justify the chain rule, injectivity composes, and the checked continuous-linear-map coercions and range_comp prove the subspace identity. No missing dependency or circular step occurs.

subproblem.title: Bi-Lipschitz images of Borel, locally H^n-finite subsets of U
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, M ⊆ ℝ^P with M Borel, M ⊆ U, and H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U, where H^n = μHE[n]. Let φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Λ-Lipschitz and Λ'-antilipschitz (|x − y| ≤ Λ'|φ(x) − φ(y)| for all x, y; Λ, Λ' ≥ 0) with φ^{-1}(U) = U. Then φ(M) is Borel, φ(M) ⊆ U, and H^n(φ(M) ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Euclid P)) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ Λ' : NNReal), MeasurableSet M → M ⊆ U → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M ∩ C) ≠ ∞) → LipschitzWith Λ φ → AntilipschitzWith Λ' φ → φ ⁻¹' U = U → MeasurableSet (φ '' M) ∧ φ '' M ⊆ U ∧ ∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → μHE[n] (φ '' M ∩ C) ≠ ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof, with the details filled in; openness of U is not used, and Lipschitz and antilipschitz constants may differ.
1. Continuity and injectivity. φ is Lipschitz, hence continuous (LipschitzWith.continuous). φ is injective: if φ(x) = φ(y) then |x − y| ≤ Λ'|φ(x) − φ(y)| = 0 (AntilipschitzWith.injective; this also covers Λ' = 0).
2. φ(M) is Borel. ℝ^P is a Polish space with its Borel σ-algebra, M is Borel, and φ is continuous on M and injective on M, so φ(M) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
3. φ(M) ⊆ U. Let y ∈ φ(M), y = φ(x) with x ∈ M. Then x ∈ U = φ^{-1}(U) (M ⊆ U and φ^{-1}(U) = U), i.e. y = φ(x) ∈ U.
4. Compact preimages. Fix a compact C ⊆ U and put K := φ^{-1}(C). C is closed and φ is continuous, so K is closed. C is bounded and diam φ^{-1}(C) ≤ Λ' diam C, so K is bounded (AntilipschitzWith.isBounded_preimage). ℝ^P is proper, so K is compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). Moreover K ⊆ φ^{-1}(U) = U (preimage_mono). Hence H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ by hypothesis.
5. Lipschitz image bound for H^n. By definition μHE[n] = c·μH[n], with c := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝ^n, μH[n]) ∈ [0, ∞) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def; the smul is multiplication by the coercion of c). For every S ⊆ ℝ^P, μH[n](φ(S)) ≤ Λ^n μH[n](S) (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with exponent d = n ≥ 0), hence H^n(φ(S)) = c·μH[n](φ(S)) ≤ c·Λ^n·μH[n](S) = Λ^n H^n(S).
6. Conclusion. φ(M) ∩ C = φ(M ∩ φ^{-1}(C)) = φ(M ∩ K) (Set.image_inter_preimage). By steps 5 and 4, H^n(φ(M) ∩ C) ≤ Λ^n H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞, since Λ^n < ∞. Together with steps 2 and 3 this proves all three claims, uniformly in n ≥ 0 and P ≥ 0.
proof_key_steps: φ is continuous (Lipschitz) and injective (antilipschitz), so φ(M) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin.
M ⊆ U = φ^{-1}(U) gives φ(M) ⊆ U.
For compact C ⊆ U, K = φ^{-1}(C) is closed and bounded (antilipschitz), hence compact, and K ⊆ φ^{-1}(U) = U.
μHE[n] = c·μH[n] and the Hausdorff Lipschitz bound give H^n(φ(S)) ≤ Λ^n H^n(S).
φ(M) ∩ C = φ(M ∩ K), so H^n(φ(M) ∩ C) ≤ Λ^n H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and conclusions match. Continuity and injectivity justify Lusin–Souslin; the preimage identity gives containment in U; antilipschitzness makes compact preimages bounded, hence compact. The normalized Hausdorff Lipschitz bound then proves local finiteness. Neither openness nor surjectivity is needed.
